fixes.why: The first eight rows after the word-row are the Pauline and later-doctrine rows (3 to 8: original sin, the three 'total depravity' rows, Romans 7). The Torah's own treatment of sin (the sin offering, confession, the Law's cases, the Day of Atonement) comes at rows 12 to 14 and 23, and the kings at 16. A reader meets the hub as a Romans 5-8 debate with the Old Testament as supporting citation, and the arc (Torah, kings and prophets, then Gospels and letters) is not visible. The ordering does not settle any question, but it does set the frame.
fixes.fix: Reorder so the Hebrew Scriptures lead: sin beside iniquity; confessing; the sin offering; sin forgiven/atoned; the Law's cases; the fathers' sins and the children; each dies for his own sin; the kings; then consequences (sin and death, sin and what follows), then the New Testament rows (Christ and our sins; sin and the law; one man; slaves/mastered/Romans 7; the sin to death). Keep the 'side by side' sets adjacent to each other.

fixes.row: Each is to die for his own sin / The fathers' sins, and the children / Sin through one man, Adam
fixes.why: The three rows and their notes are framed as one question, 'original sin and inherited guilt'. That is a later doctrinal category. Deut 24:16, 2 Kgs 14:6 and Ezek 18 are about judicial and covenant responsibility (who is put to death, whether the exiles may blame their fathers), and Exod 34:7 and the confessions are about the generations of a covenant people. Reading them as three answers to the doctrine reads it back into texts that do not ask it. The Romans 5 row does ask something like it.
fixes.fix: Keep the three rows, but in the two Old Testament rows drop 'original sin and inherited guilt' from the notes and say what the text asks: 'who bears a person's sin: the one who sinned, or his father or his children'. Name the doctrinal question only in the Romans 5 / Ps 51:5 row, and say there that the Old Testament rows are set beside it because readers bring them to it, not because they pose it.

fixes.row: Sin through one man, Adam; sinful from conception; "born in utter sin"
fixes.why: John 9:34 is a hostile retort of the Pharisees to the man healed, answering the disciples' question (9:2) and Jesus' answer (9:3). The scene is cut across two rows, so the retort stands as a witness for a doctrine and Jesus' answer sits in another row. The label's 'born in utter sin' also presents an insult as a pole of the question. 'Adam' in the label is named only in Rom 5:14.
fixes.fix: Move John 9:34 into the 'each is to die for his own sin' row beside 9:2-3 (note: the Pharisees' retort follows Jesus' answer), so the scene is whole; remove '"born in utter sin"' from this row's label, which becomes 'Sin through one man; sinful from conception' (Rom 5:12, 5:14, 5:16, 5:19, Ps 51:5). Note that Adam is named in Rom 5:14.

fixes.row: The fathers' sins, and the children
fixes.why: The note says 'the generations confess their fathers' sins as their own (Lam 5:7; Jer 14:20; ...)'. Lam 5:7 is a complaint ('Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment'), not a confession; Lam 5:16 is the confession. The note says more than the verse.
fixes.fix: Rewrite: 'the generations confess their fathers' sins with their own (Jer 14:20; Neh 9:2; Dan 9:16; Ps 106:6); in Lam 5:7 they say they bear their fathers' punishment'. Ezek 18:14 stays; add that it is the son who does not do likewise.

fixes.row: "All under sin", "slaves to sin", "dead in your trespasses and sins" / Sin to be mastered... / "Sin living in me"
fixes.why: The three rows' notes name 'what is sometimes called total depravity', a Reformed label for a systematic claim; none of the verses asserts a total inability and Gen 4:7 (Cain, with a choice put to him) sits in the same series as Rom 6. Rom 8:10 ('your body is dead because of sin') is about the body's death in a believer, not slavery or binding of the will, so it misfits row 6. Rom 7:14 is in two of the three rows.
fixes.fix: Name the series by what the verses say: 'How sin holds a person, and how the text speaks of resisting it', and mention the doctrinal label once, in the note, as a label readers use. Move Rom 8:10 to the 'Sin and death' row only. Keep Rom 7:14 in the Romans 7 row and remove it from row 6 (or leave the cross-reference in the note).

fixes.row: Sin to be mastered, resisted, thrown off
fixes.why: The row puts Gen 4:7 (an instruction to Cain, 'you must master it') under one verb with Paul's 'dead to sin' and 'set free', which are said of those in Christ and speak of a different kind of freedom (status, not exertion). The note says the row is about verbs; the label presents them as one thing. Gen 4:7 is also the first use of the sin word in the Bible and is buried in the middle of a Pauline row.
fixes.fix: Give Gen 4:7 its own place in the Old Testament group (with Gen 13:13, 39:9, Exod 32:30 as the earliest uses: 'Sin first named') or at least make it the row's stated lead and add to the note that Gen 4:7 is addressed to Cain and Rom 6 to believers, so the verbs are not the same act.

fixes.row: Sin and death / Sin and what follows
fixes.why: Both rows are 'a consequence named in the verse with the sin'; death is the most severe consequence named. A reader cannot tell why 'swept away in all their sins' (Num 16:26) is in the second row and 'die in his sin' (Ezek 3:20) in the first. Row 10's label is also the vaguest on the page ('what follows').
fixes.fix: Merge into 'Sin and its consequence', with the death verses leading and the Leviticus 26, Jeremiah and Micah verses after, or keep two rows but label row 10 'Sin and the punishment named beside it' and say in both notes that they overlap.

fixes.why: The four examples a reader sees first are all New Testament, and Rom 5:12 is already the lead of the Romans 5 row and a third time in the 'no one without sin' row. 22 of the 41 verses are Hebrew Scriptures (Ezek 18, 33; Deut 24:16; 2 Sam 12:13; Num 18:22) and speak of dying 'for' or 'in' a sin on the Torah's and the prophets' terms.
fixes.fix: Set the examples to Ezek 18:24 or 18:20 (or Ezek 33:14), 2 Sam 12:13 ('you will not die'), Rom 6:23, Jas 1:15 so the Hebrew Scriptures are heard first and not only as precursors. Note that Num 18:22 is 'bear sin ... die' in the Hebrew where the Berean prints 'incur guilt and die' (the original arbitrates).

fixes.row: "If someone sins": the Law's cases, sinning unintentionally; sinning deliberately
fixes.why: Answering the worker's question: yes, it reads as a ruling. Heb 10:26 is an New Testament verse filed under the Torah's heading, beside Num 15:30, so the row says Hebrews is working the Num 15 category of defiant sin. Hebrews itself does not cite Num 15 here (10:28 cites the law of Moses on a witness's evidence, Deut 17:6). The pairing is the builder's, and it is exactly where Lutheran, Reformed, Wesleyan and Baptist readers part on falling away. Also Num 15:30 lacks the sin word in Hebrew (the note admits it). The same verse, Heb 10:26, is a verb-form verse that most readers would look for next to the unforgivable sin.
fixes.fix: Take Heb 10:26 out of this row and put it in 'A sin that leads to death; a sin that is not forgiven' with the existing note that readers part on whether it describes a believer who falls away; say there only that the verse speaks of 'no further sacrifice', not of the sin being unforgiven. Keep Num 15:30 in the Law's cases row (it names sins done 'defiantly' in the Law's own cases), with its note about the Hebrew. Retitle the row 'If someone sins: the Law's cases, sinning unintentionally and defiantly'.

fixes.row: Sin forgiven, atoned for... / The sin offering
fixes.why: The two largest rows (109 and 121) draw on the same Leviticus 4 to 16 and Numbers verses; a reader who opens one finds the same passages in the other. The two together are 230 of the noun form's 467 verse slots. The Day of Atonement (Lev 16) is cut into four rows (1, 12, 13, 14).
fixes.fix: Keep both, but make the split honest: row 13 gets the forgiveness language in its own right (Ps 32, Isa 43:25, Jer 31:34, Mic 7:19, Gospels, 1 John) and row 14 the sacrifice. Remove from row 13 the verses that are also in row 14 and say only 'make atonement' in the note, with a pointer to row 14. Or put the 27 Levitical verses that are in both under a single sub-heading.

fixes.row: The sin offering; a sacrifice for sin
fixes.why: The row sets the Hebrew chatta't, rendered 'sin offering', beside Greek phrases the Berean renders 'offering for sin' and 'sacrifice for sin'. The Greek of Rom 8:3 is peri hamartias, which is 'concerning sin' in many translations; the Berean has chosen the 'offering' reading. The row therefore rests on one translation's choice. The Septuagint uses the same Greek phrase for the sin offering, so the link is real for Hebrews, but the page should say it is a link, not equate the words.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: 'Rom 8:3 is here because the Berean prints "as an offering for sin"; the Greek is peri hamartias ("concerning sin"), the phrase the Greek Old Testament also uses for the sin offering. Other translations read "to deal with sin".' Same for Heb 5:1 and 10:12 if included.

fixes.why: The text's own links are cut: 1 Pet 2:24 quotes Isaiah 53, and the 'bore our sins' phrase sits in a separate row (sin and death) from Isa 53:12. A reader of the Christ row meets 'bore our sins' with no thread back to the servant who 'bore the sin of many' or to Aaron who 'put them on the goat's head'. That is the story's own arc and is cut apart. At the same time, filing Isa 53 under the Christ row would put Jesus in Isaiah's text.
fixes.fix: Add a pointer in the note: 'Where the verses quote or echo the Old Testament they say so (1 Pet 2:22-25 on Isaiah 53); the Isaiah 53:12 and Leviticus 16:21 verses are in the rows on sin and death and confessing sin.' Do not move them.

fixes.row: The sins of the kings / "He caused Israel to sin"
fixes.why: These two rows are the same verses by the same refrain (the noun and the causative verb of one phrase). Nine of the verb row's 15 verses are also in the noun row. The builder says so ('the verb of the phrase in the row for the kings' sins'). They are one pattern split by the part of speech of a lemma, which is the index shape the project avoids. The refrain is the editor's verdict formula and is one of the clearest pieces of the Kings' structure.
fixes.fix: Merge into one row 'The sins of the kings: "the sin Jeroboam caused Israel to commit"' (about 36 verses), listing the noun verses and the 'caused Israel/Judah to sin' verses together, with Jer 32:35 as the prophetic echo. This also brings the page to 25 rows.

fixes.row: Sinners and the righteous / Christ Jesus and sinners
fixes.why: 'Sinners' as a noun has an Old Testament life of its own (the men of Sodom 'wicked and sinners against the LORD', Ps 1:1, Prov 13:21, Isa 33:14). The page shows two NT-leaning rows and drops the OT 'sinners' row (the report says it was cut to stay near 25), so a reader learns the Gospels' 'tax collectors and sinners' without the category it contrasts with. Matt 9:13 is also an example in both rows.
fixes.fix: Fold the dropped OT 'sinners' verses (Gen 13:13, Num 16:38, Ps 1:1, Ps 26:9, Ps 104:35, Prov 1:10, Isa 33:14) into 'Sinners and the righteous' so the row leads with Ps 1 and Prov 13:21; change its examples to Ps 1:1, Prov 13:21, Gen 13:13, Luke 15:7, and keep Matt 9:13 only in the 'Christ and sinners' row.

fixes.row: There is no one who does not sin / "Anyone born of God ... cannot go on sinning" / "Do not sin"
fixes.why: The three-row set is introduced as 'whether a believer sins'. The Old Testament verses in it (Solomon's prayer, Ecclesiastes, Proverbs 20:9, Exod 20:20) are about human beings and the people, and say nothing about the Christian question. They are filed under it by the framing of the note.
fixes.fix: Open the note of the first row with the Old Testament: 'In the Hebrew Scriptures this is said of every human being (1 Kgs 8:46, Eccl 7:20, Prov 20:9). In 1 John it is said to believers, and where traditions part on whether a believer sins, the page takes no side.' Same sentence in the other two rows.

fixes.row: Sinned against the LORD, against God
fixes.why: The rule 'the verse itself names the LORD' keeps out Ps 51:4 ('Against You, You only, have I sinned') and Solomon's prayer ('they sin against You'), both addressed to the LORD in the verse's own scene, while Jer 14:20 (also 'against You') is kept because 'O LORD' appears in the verse. The result cuts the central confession in the Psalms from the row about whom sin is against.
fixes.fix: By hand, add Ps 51:4 and 1 Kgs 8:33, 8:46, 2 Chr 6:24 with a note that the LORD is named in the prayer they belong to (Ps 51 is a psalm of David addressed to God). If the page keeps the rule, put a pointer to Ps 51:4 in the note.

fixes.row: Sinned against another: a neighbor, a brother, one's own body
fixes.why: 1 Cor 8:12 ('you sin against Christ') and Luke 15:18, 21 ('against heaven and against you') are against Christ and heaven, not 'another' in the label's sense; the note admits it. 'Against heaven' is a Jewish circumlocution for God, and the row presents it as one more neighbor.
fixes.fix: Move 1 Cor 8:12 and the 'against heaven' halves of Luke 15:18, 21 into a short note ('also against Christ, against heaven') or into the 'against the LORD, against God' row with the note that 'heaven' is a way of speaking of God.

fixes.row: Sin beside iniquity, transgression, trespass, lawlessness, wickedness
fixes.why: The note is right that the words are kept apart. But the label starts 'Sin beside ...' and then the row is 74 verses of every pairing, with the one 'sin is lawlessness' definition (1 John 3:4) and a verse that gathers Hebrew terms in a list (Exod 34:7) side by side. A reader will take the row as a synonym list. The hub has no way to show which pair in each verse is the pair.
fixes.fix: Keep the label but add to the note: 'Only 1 John 3:4 says that one is the other; the rest set them beside each other, as in Exod 34:7 and Ps 32:5.' Put 1 John 3:4 first in the eg or mark it.

worker_points.point: Original sin: is 'Sin through one man, Adam; sinful from conception' a label that leans? Adam named only in Rom 5:14
worker_points.why: The label stacks three claims; 'Adam' is fair for Rom 5:14 but not for Ps 51:5 or John 9:34, and the retort of John 9:34 belongs with John 9:2-3. See the fixes for the Romans 5 row and the Old Testament framing.

worker_points.point: John 9:2-3 in row 4 is about a man's blindness, not a law of guilt
worker_points.why: The note says so, but then the scene is cut: with 9:34 moved there, the three verses form one scene. Keep the note; it is fair.

worker_points.point: Ezek 18:14 in row 5 though it speaks for row 4 too
worker_points.why: In 18:14 the son does not copy the father, which is the Ezek 18 principle, not the covenant visiting of Exod 34:7. Keep it in row 4 ('each dies for his own sin') and leave a cross-reference in row 5.

worker_points.point: Rows 6, 7, 8: row 7 mixes who is addressed (Cain, believers)
worker_points.why: Say so in the note; do not leave the label as one thing. See the fix for the mastered row.

worker_points.point: Row 17 mixes Old Testament 'no one' with 1 John
worker_points.why: The note names it, but the opening framing is the Christian question. Lead with the Hebrew Scriptures' own sense.

worker_points.point: Heb 10:26 in the Law's cases row beside Num 15:30 reads as a ruling
worker_points.why: It does. The pairing is not in either text. Move Heb 10:26 to the unforgivable-sin row with the existing note.

worker_points.point: Rom 8:3 in row 14 because the Berean prints 'offering for sin'; the Greek is 'concerning sin'
worker_points.why: Keep the verse, since the Septuagint uses the phrase for the sin offering, but state the Greek and other translations in the note.

worker_points.point: 2 Cor 5:21 ('Him', 'knew no sin') in the Christ row: is the 'by hand' honest?
worker_points.why: The verse's preceding clause (5:20) names Christ and 5:21 'Him who knew no sin' is plain in context. The note states the basis. Keep.

worker_points.point: Num 18:22 shown in the Hebrew only (the Berean prints 'guilt')
worker_points.why: The original arbitrates. Add the asterisk or an 'in the Hebrew' note so a reader who looks for 'sin' in the English is not misled; I confirmed the Berean text of 18:22 does not say 'sin'.

worker_points.point: Heb 12:4 label fixed after the check
worker_points.why: 'mastered, resisted, thrown off' now shows in the example; 1 Pet 4:1 ('done with sin') fits 'dead to sin'.

worker_points.point: Row 20 does not place 'against You/Me/Him' verses
worker_points.why: The rule is careful, but it cuts Ps 51:4 from the row about whom sin is against. Add by hand.

worker_points.point: Rows 16 and 24 built from the same Jeroboam rule
worker_points.why: Merge; the nine shared verses show it is one pattern.

worker_points.point: h5512 Sin (the wilderness) on the card's word list
worker_points.why: A place name that is not the sin word; leaving it out of the hub is right. The card's owner should remove it from the card.

worker_points.point: Lev 6:3 shows the mismatched Hebrew word strip on the verse card
worker_points.why: A server issue, not a hub fault; the Berean text is correct. It should be fixed before row 23 is shown (the Lev 5:20-26 / 6:1-7 offset).

missing.what: The Day of Atonement and the live goat: Lev 16:21-22 ('all their iniquities and transgressions, all their sins ... the goat will carry on itself') as its own place, rather than scattered over four rows, so the Torah's centre of sin and its removal can be seen whole.

The golden calf as the Torah's pivotal story of sin (Exod 32:30-34, Deut 9:16-21): 'you have committed a great sin' is the Pentateuch's own account of the sin that nearly ends the covenant. The worker dropped the row; the verses appear only as scattered members of forgiveness and 'against the LORD' rows.

The first uses of the sin word in the Bible, in Genesis: Gen 4:7 (Cain), Gen 13:13 (Sodom 'sinners against the LORD'), Gen 18:20 (Sodom's 'sin ... very grave'), Gen 39:9, Gen 42:22. The story's own opening arc of sin (Cain, Sodom, Joseph) is not visible because Gen 4:7 is inside a Pauline row.

examples_checked: 26 of 26 rows' examples show their label; row 3 label is carried by Rom 5:12, 5:19 and Ps 51:5, but John 9:34 shows only 'born in utter sin' (an insult, not a claim); row 9's examples show it; row 21's examples show it; row 17's 1 John 1:8 shows 'no sin' not 'sinned' (fine as the label is a list)
summary: The hub is largely true to its verses and its notes keep the page neutral, but it frames the Hebrew Scriptures through Romans 5-8 and the believer-sins question, lets the order put later doctrine ahead of the Torah's own treatment of sin, and splits the Day of Atonement, the golden calf and the Kings' refrain across rows that overlap. Fix the framing and order, move John 9:34 and Heb 10:26 to where their scenes and arguments are, merge the two Jeroboam rows, and it should ship.
